title: WPSS/1703/2024 of NEELAM LAL Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND

paras.text:
2024:UHC:6421
HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Writ Petition Service Single No. 1703 of 2024
05th September, 2024
Neelam Lal --Petitioner
Versus
State Of Uttarakhand and others --Respondents
----------------------------------------------------------------------
Presence:-
Mr. B N Molakhi, Advocate for the petitioner.
Mr. Bhupendra Koranga, learned Brief Holder for the State.
Mr. Nishant K. Adhikari, learned counsel i/b Mr. Ramji Srivastava,
learned counsel for respondent no.3-Selection Board.
----------------------------------------------------------------------
 Heard learned Counsel for the parties.
2. Petitioner has sought for writ of certiorari
seeking to quash the impugned final ineligibility list
dated 12.09.2023 issued by respondent no.3 (Annexure
No.14), qua petitioner, whereby petitioner has been
declared ineligible for the post of Nursing Officer.
3. It is submitted by learned Counsel that
petitioner submitted her candidature pursuant to the
advertisement dated 03.01.2023 issued by respondent
no.3 for supplying vacancies on the post of Nursing
Officer (Male/Female) in the State. The last date of
submission of application form was initially 01.02.2023
which was later on extended to 15.02.2023. Petitioner
submitted her candidature on 10.02.2023. After
document verification, it was found that petitioner's
application form was lacking, inasmuch as, the same was
not accompanied with a valid registration certificate with
'Uttarakhand Nurses and Midwives Council', and
accordingly, petitioner was found ineligible and her name
was mentioned in the ineligibility list dated 12.09.2023.
1

2024:UHC:6421
4. Learned counsel for petitioner submits that
petitioner possesses the qualification for being appointed
as Nursing Officer in the State. She fulfills the eligibility
criteria; so far as objection regarding non-possession the
registration certificate with 'Uttarakhand Nurses and
Midwives Council' is concerned, the said certificate was
subsequently provided to respondent no.3-Selection Body
by petitioner on 13.06.2023 after she was registered with
the aforesaid Council. It is further submitted that
petitioner had moved an application for registration in
the Council on 30.01.2023, and the fees for registration
was already deposited, and therefore, the order of
treating the petitioner as ineligible is faulty and cannot
sustain in the eyes of law.
5. Per contra, learned Counsel appearing for
respondent no.3 submits that the eligibility of a
candidate is to be seen on the last date of submission of
application form, and petitioner did not possess the valid
qualification on the relevant date, and thus, there was
nothing wrong in rejecting petitioner's candidature
treating her as ineligible. It is further submitted by
learned counsel for respondent no.3 that pursuant to
aforesaid advertisement dated 03.01.2023, selection
process has been concluded and appointments have
already been made, and therefore, petitioner has
approached this Court after a considerable period and
her writ petition is hopelessly time barred.
6. Having considered the submissions of learned
Counsel for the parties and having perused the record of
the case, the submissions made by learned Counsel for
respondent no.3 found favours with this Court, and
accordingly, this Court does not find any arbitrariness or
unreasonableness in the action of selecting body in
rejecting petitioner's candidature.
2

2024:UHC:6421
7. The petition fails and the same is dismissed as
the threshold itself. No order as to costs.
 (Pankaj Purohit, J.)
05.09.2024
Rdang
3
RAJEEV DANG
